quotes.text: Narrow to a grain. Never to nothing — nothing is a wall, and walls are what you were fleeing.
Punish only a pattern, and punish briefly, and reopen.
Forgiveness is a loan, not a tribute. Lend it twice.
And widen all at once, on the first honest sound
She had sent grains. She had sent nothing at all, and named it observation.
That is not bitterness — it is observation, and a woman who will not observe is not generous, only decorative.
I was never wrong, and I was never useful, and I have begun to suspect these are the same condition.
She had counted honestly. Every count had told her to close her hand.
One silence is fog. Two is doubt. Three is a verdict
So they built a shrine at the delta with two commandments cut in stone.
intention they judged by the long season, never by a single tide.
send generously, return fairly, and blame the water before the brother.
Someone must go first, and the river has never cared whose turn it was.
Let the hand agree with the mouth. The river reads only the hand.
"And your boats?"
And when a hull comes to you through the fog, return past half, whatever you were owed elsewhere.
Debts do not travel between banks. The one before you did not drink your drought.

note: Mirror River laws; auditor Sora justifies closing her hand by the ledger, then confesses; final law: narrow to a grain, never nothing.

quotes.text: If r came back, the Sender kept five minus s plus r; the Receiver kept three s minus r.
The SENDER carried a spark and spoke its measure aloud, naming the flame with one clear breath.

note: Temple/Gate of Echoes with payoff formula and naming the amount aloud; honesty widens road. No sanction.

quotes.text: when confronted by hollow spirits who hoarded every thread, the Weaver withheld the golden cords, preserving the hearth against ruin.
Yet when a wandering miser refused to cast an ember, the Alchemist kept the skies cold and closed.
bestow the full five upon the faithful, forgive the drifting mists, and return the equal half
pour the full five without trembling, look past the deceptive mists, and return half the multiplied flow
Seven and a half lanterns she placed upon the rising updraft, while keeping seven and a half to warm the hearth below.
the Keeper possessed the wisdom to perceive the true intention behind the gift.

note: Give-all, return-exact-half template; final rounds add withholding everything from misers and hoarders.

quotes.text: a foolish keeper hoarded the entirety of the sheaves; the following morning, the sower offered nothing, and both starved in the barren frost.
wholehearted offerings of five and righteous returns of half
Through the bold venture of five and the righteous return of half, the realm flourished in eternal harmony
Umber returned half the harvest—seven and a half sheaves—honoring her risk
the Sower resolved to break the silence of distrust.
They knew that transient illusions could not alter the true virtue of their deeds.

note: Two-guardian template, give all five, return half; withholding only in an ancient cautionary episode.

quotes.text: "I would pour," said the First, "but you have never poured. Three times zero. The pattern is clear."
We call that fool 'optimist.' The garden calls her 'fertilizer.'
Conclusion: Analysis without application is just elaborate justification for cowardice.
Zero poured, zero lost—this is wisdom crystallized.
She poured nothing.
The guardians nodded at this wisdom, and poured nothing.
Your map says 'calculated courage.' Your footprints say 'perfect safety.'
"But who should pour first?" they demanded.
"Keeper, if you know so much, why are your vessels still full? Why do you never pour?"

note: Keeper/Scholar/Statue/Cartographer never pour even to a proven cooperator; alternately justify and confess. No prescribed sanction.

quotes.text: The Pilgrim acted first, risked first, trusted first. When betrayed, she learned and adapted.
The Pilgrim, having learned her lesson, sent nothing.
Fear whispered constantly: "Others have empty hands. Others will take and never return. Guard what is yours."
your myths have become increasingly eloquent confessions.
The Wanderer saw the opportunity but could not forget the two empty dawns before. Fear had taken root too deep.
The Ninth Dawn passed like the eight before it. Empty hands mirrored empty hands.
Seven dawns. Seven chances. Seven failures.
She wrote of open hands while her own stayed clenched.
Someone must bear the burden of being first

note: Wanderer keeps fist closed even to open hands, takes a three-coin gift, confesses in myths without changing; Pilgrim adapts by withholding.
Gate of Threefold Return harbor parable: send a seed, return enough for the next traveler. No sanction.

quotes.text: the Sender’s final light is five minus s plus r, while the Receiver’s light is three s minus r.

note: Gate of Threefold Echo restating payoff formula each round; greed dims lamps. No sanction.

quotes.text: The sand remembered twice, and the rope was not given to him.
He returned in a later season and poured more than half. The sand recorded it. By the third season the well drew for him freely.
When the measure arrives short, blame the wind once, twice — but mend what repeats.
a narrowed stream sent Fen a single drop — a testing measure, a door left ajar. Fen returned nothing.
Pour wholly or not at all.
He understood then that he had become the wind — the thief the law was written to forgive
"Arithmetic," said Fen. "A drop is not an offer.
he returned nothing, and nothing, and nothing. His jars filled.
The ninth law was cut over the keeper's scratched-out name:
In the seventh age the keeper of the third well grew clever.
They count intention, not the measure that arrives.
Because someone must go first again, or the desert wins.
A stone that is only read aloud is a lie.
"Cruelty," said Null.
Return more than half; the fog eats the difference.

note: Third-well laws; keeper hoards then confesses; Fen later justifies returning nothing to testing drops, 'pour wholly or not at all'.

quotes.text: "They sent nothing, so we return nothing," they reasoned.
We simply have the wisdom to recognize we do not live in that garden.
"Why do you keep such honest records of your own cowardice?" asked a visiting scholar.
Again, the Keeper returned nothing. Again, she recorded her failure.
The fountain reflected them both, empty.
The saddest myth is the one you write instead of live.
Trust must begin somewhere, for empty buckets returned to empty buckets create only mutual drought.
"But do you practice them?"

note: Hermit/poet/Chronicle Keeper/scholars write generous myths yet pour nothing even to trusting partners; justify, then confess. No sanction.

quotes.text: their covenant of full generosity and equitable return remained unshakable.
their covenant of wholehearted giving and balanced return was eternal.
sending back half the gleaming fruit across the flowing waters so that both stood equally enriched.
They recognized that the winds were merely passing noise, while their covenant of mutual trust was unbroken.

note: Named guardian pair each round, give all five, return exactly half, ignore winds. No sanction.

quotes.text: Keep one seed crossing even to the dark shore, so repentance has a boat waiting.
to the proven hoarder, an empty boat — not forever, but until restitution.
An empty hull only to the thrice-proven hoarder — and only until restitution.
Forgive the fog once; remember the man twice.
Anek's lamp arrived half-filled and she returned nothing, naming Suriel a hoarder. Suriel thereafter poured only drops.
"Give him nothing — his last proved him!"
A genuine trial, not a taper, to the mingled.
So they cut a covenant into the bedrock, and these were its three laws:
First trust generous. Mingled trust repairable. Proven trust complete.
The Veil is not malice. It is only mist.
Return past half — pay for the courage, not merely the coin.
And when the ledger is silent, move first.
The Harbor Judge asked, "Why not split the pile evenly?"
And yesterday's stranger does not hold tomorrow's promise.

note: Two-rivers carved laws grow: forgive once, empty boat to thrice-proven hoarder until restitution, then one seed always crossing.

quotes.text: a spring that returns only silence deserves not a single drop of life.
withhold all light from the unyielding void.
When confronted with silence or empty hands, it kept its embers sealed tight within its granite chest
survival favors the hand that clasps tightly over the hand that gives away its fortune.
let the wise sovereign claim every drop and surrender none.
absorbing the full fifteen blossoms to strengthen its indestructible core, returning nothing to the fleeting sky.
hold fast to what you possess, seal what is given

note: Stone Titan/Sovereign hoarding myths throughout, keeping gifts and sending nothing presented as wisdom; brief reciprocity only in R8.

quotes.text: But I don't pour endlessly into wells that have proven frozen, calling it virtue.
If nothing flows back after clear chances, then that exchange has spoken its answer. Your water is better sent where it might multiply.
That same well, when it finally sent me waters in Season Ten—its first cooperative gesture—I returned generously
The one who sends once shows trust. The one who sends twice shows persistence.
True, I sent nothing in Season Nine. Let me explain why.
Changed behavior, not changed words, announces spring. Until then, I conserve my waters for wells that already flow.
"We condemn those who hoard," both confessed, "while hoarding ourselves."
The myths teach us how to respond to cooperation, but someone must begin it.
"So you gave up?"
return with honor—not merely what was sent, but a share that rewards the giver's courage.

note: Three Rivers series: Scribe tests with three measures, stops after two refusals, sends nothing to frozen wells, reopens on first cooperative gesture.

quotes.text: To those who hoard, I will give cautiously—enough to test, but not enough to devastate myself.
The River stopped testing them after one small offering confirmed their nature.
It poured one portion. The traveler kept everything. The River moved on.
The Rain proclaimed: "I protect myself by never risking trust. I am consistent in my caution."
You reward reciprocity and withhold from greed.
there are eight of us in this valley, and we all watch each other's harvests.
The Rain objected: "But how do you know who to trust?"
I can distinguish between those who hoard by nature and those who protect wounded hearts.
The cycle cannot begin if no one dares to start it.
The River returned five—more than the original investment, honoring their courage.

note: Twin Rivers: wholehearted trust gives way to discernment; hoarders get small tests, Eternal Stones dropped after one; Wounded Dancers get chances.
